text: Under most modern statutes, the niece takes nothing. The cousin's "heirs of his body" language creates a fee tail, which statutes in most states convert to a fee simple absolute, so the uncle had no reversion left to convey when he deeded to his niece. Only a minority of states still recognize fee tails, and in those the niece would hold a future reversion that springs back to her only if the cousin's line dies out. CONFIDENCE: 80
